text: This is AivaCare, an agentic AI platform for continuous care of fatty liver disease, built as a working prototype for LiverWell Clinic. In the next five minutes, I'll show what we built, how it works under the hood, and the experience from each persona's point of view.

Today, patients like John Miller, forty-eight, with fatty liver disease, see their hepatologist every three months. Between visits, his lab results, medical records and Apple Watch data sit in separate systems, and nobody is watching the trend. Concerning changes are noticed late. AivaCare moves the clinic to continuous care: monitor between visits, guide the patient, and bring the right findings to the care team, with physicians in control.

We built three entry points on one platform: a patient mobile app, a patient web portal, and a clinician care dashboard, plus presenter controls for demos. It runs on Google Cloud with synthetic data, uses a FHIR record as the system of record, and uses Claude as the AI.

Under the hood, the principle is simple: rules decide, AI explains, physicians approve. A deterministic rules engine watches labs and wearable data, for example a FIB-4 score above 2.67. Two Claude agents handle conversation: a Patient Care Agent and a Clinician Copilot. They reach data only through governed MCP tool servers, bound to the signed-in user. Guidance comes from clinician-approved content through RAG, with citations. And a LangGraph workflow manages each escalation, pausing until a physician approves.

Let's start with John. His home page combines lab results from the clinic with daily data from his watch. His ALT came down from 82 to 44, but it's rising again, while his weight creeps up and his steps fall. His FIB-4 score is still in the low-risk band.

John asks the assistant: why is my ALT high, and what should I eat? Watch the steps: it checks his trend data and searches the approved guidance. The answer quotes his exact values, and each recommendation cites a LiverWell guide, so John only gets clinician-approved advice.

John can also upload a lab report. Claude reads the PDF, extracts each result with its units and reference range, and the platform validates them. John confirms the values before they're saved to his record, with provenance back to the document.

Now, new results arrive from the lab feed. The rules engine calculates a FIB-4 of 2.87, above the 2.67 threshold, and a high-priority alert appears live in the care team's queue, with a 24-hour deadline. Seconds later, the Copilot's review is ready.

Sam, the care coordinator, triages the queue. Sam sees the full picture and can acknowledge the alert, but clinical decisions are reserved for physicians, so the actions show as awaiting physician approval.

Doctor Patel opens the Patient 360 view. She sees the rule evidence, the trends, and the AI review: a headline, findings with exact values, and citations to the clinic's fibrosis pathway. She asks the Copilot what changed in the last ninety days. It pulls the record through governed tools, and answers with dates and values.

The proposed care-plan actions are only drafts. Doctor Patel removes one, adds a repeat liver panel in four weeks, and approves. Only now does anything change: the care plan is updated, the task closes, and every step is audited.
Back on John's phone, a plain-language follow-up from his care team has already arrived, and his care plan shows the new actions.

Safety comes first. When John writes, my eyes look yellow today, the red-flag guardrail bypasses the AI completely. He gets urgent-care instructions instantly, and a high-priority alert goes to the care team.
For governance, clinicians can review the versioned rule catalog, and a full audit trail of every alert, AI review and decision.

That's AivaCare: continuous monitoring, grounded AI support for patients, and AI-assisted, physician-approved interventions, built on open standards. The next steps are clinical sign-off of the rules and content, integration with the clinic's EMR and lab feeds, and a pilot with consenting patients.
